title: Let Claude determine summary format instead of predefined structure
description: Currently the summary uses a rigid predefined structure (key moments, Q&A, emerging themes, key insights, momentum, observer's perspective) enforced via a tool schema. In a previous version, Claude had more freedom to determine the appropriate format/sections based on the actual meeting content. Revert to letting Claude decide the summary structure — the output should feel more natural and tailored to each transcript rather than forcing every meeting into the same template.

title: Extract 'pearls' — distilled truths from meeting transcripts
description:
## What
Add a second-pass agent that extracts 'pearls' from meetings — units of wise, distilled meaning about what's really happening beneath the surface.

## Pearl characteristics
- **Distilled truths**: Patterns, dynamics, or wisdom people might not notice (not action items or surface-level insights)
- **3-7 per meeting**: Curated set, enough to cover key dynamics without overwhelming
- **Mix of personalized + universal**: Some shaped by who's asking and what they care about, some objective observations anyone would value
- **Optionally grounded**: Cite specific moments/quotes when they strengthen the pearl, omit when it speaks for itself

## Example pearls
- "Your team consistently defers technical decisions to whoever speaks loudest, not whoever has the most context"
- "Sarah's questions are consistently redirected — she may be raising concerns the group isn't ready to hear"
- "Budget discussions stall every time — this is the third meeting where the same objection surfaces without resolution" (cross-meeting)

## Agent design
- Separate Claude call that receives BOTH the transcript AND the generated summary
- Builds on the summary — can identify what it missed or go deeper on what it surfaced
- Runs after summary generation completes (not in parallel)

## Cross-meeting awareness
- Agent should have access to past meeting pearls/summaries (when available) to spot recurring patterns
- e.g., "This is the third meeting where decision-making stalls around budget topics"

## UI
- Displayed in a sidebar alongside the summary (both visible at once)

## Data model considerations
- Needs its own type/schema (pearl text, optional grounding quotes, personalized vs universal flag)
- Should be stored alongside summaries in the DB
- Design for cross-meeting querying from the start

title: Recognize and adapt to meeting structure
description:
## User Story
As a user, I want the AI to recognize and adapt to different meeting structures (Q&A, brainstorm, standup, etc.) so summaries match how the conversation actually flowed.

## User Quote
> "I want the AI to pay attention to the structure of the meeting. So here, it's clear that there was a central question, and then there were answers to those to that question."

## Requirements
- AI identifies meeting structure type (Q&A, brainstorm, presentation, discussion, standup, etc.)
- Summary format adapts to detected structure:
  - Q&A → question-answer format (related to context-keeper-ej2)
  - Brainstorms → idea clusters
  - Standups → per-person updates
  - Presentations → key points + audience reactions
- Detected structure surfaced to user (e.g., "This looks like a Q&A session")
- User can potentially override if detection is wrong

## Relationship
Broader capability that subsumes context-keeper-ej2 (central question lead-in). ej2 is the specific Q&A case; this is the general framework. Kept separate because ej2 is a concrete, shippable improvement while this is a larger architectural effort.

## Technical Approach
- Add a structure-detection step to the summary pipeline
- Structure type informs the summary generation prompt
- Could be a lightweight first-pass Claude call or part of the main prompt

title: Replace summary lead paragraph with central question + attributed answers
description:
## User Story
As a user, I want the summary's opening paragraph replaced with the meeting's central question and speaker-attributed answers, so I can immediately grasp the meeting's focus.

## User Quote
> "I think something that I would enjoy, instead of this whole paragraph of text, is just something like, like, central question that that was, like, leading the meeting."

## Scope
This is about the **lead-in** of the summary only, not restructuring the entire summary.

## Requirements
- Replace the opening narrative paragraph with:
  1. The meeting's central question — highlighted, formatted distinctly (italics or different styling)
  2. Key answers organized by speaker with direct quotes in bullet points
- Rest of the summary continues as normal after the structured lead
- Direct quotes preferred over paraphrasing in the lead section

## Technical Approach
Modify the summary generation prompt to:
1. Identify the central question driving the meeting
2. Extract key speaker-attributed responses
3. Format as structured lead, then continue with standard summary

## Relationship
Related to meeting structure recognition (context-keeper-eh6) but scoped tighter — this is specifically about the opening section format.

title: Tag-first pearl selection workflow
description:
## User Story
As a user, I want to first select from generated concept tags and then have pearls generated based on my selections, so I have more control over what gets extracted.

## User Quote
> "I feel like even just the tags themselves could be the thing that I that it shows. And then I and I'm like, keep these ones... And then, based on what I picked, it gives me the pearl."

## UX Flow (Refined)

### On Generate
1. User clicks Generate
2. Modal appears **immediately** over the summary view
   - Title: "What themes are relevant to you?"
   - Subtitle: "Themes are being generated..."
   - Loading state while tags extract
3. Summary streams behind the modal (both run in parallel)
4. Tags populate in the modal when ready (10-15 concept tags as selectable chips)
5. User can also add custom tags via text input

### Path A — User engages with modal
- Selects tags → clicks "Generate pearls" → modal closes → pearls fill sidebar
- "Skip — generate without focus" option generates unfocused pearls

### Path B — User dismisses modal (click outside / Escape)
- Modal closes, tags **migrate to the sidebar** (not lost)
- Sidebar shows the tag selector inline instead of pearls
- User browses summary at their own pace
- Selects tags from sidebar whenever ready → pearls replace tags in sidebar

### Key UX Principles
- **No dead air**: Modal appears immediately, both streams progress in parallel
- **Progressive disclosure**: Content arrives as it's ready
- **User control**: Dismiss = defer, not lose. Skip = unfocused pearls.
- **Sidebar is always useful**: Shows either pearls (selected) or tags (deferred)
- **No refinement loop for v1**: One-shot generation, re-generation is a later feature

## Technical Approach
- **Parallelize**: Start tag extraction at the same time as (or immediately after) summary generation begins — tags only need the transcript, not the completed summary
- First AI call: extract 10-15 concept tags from transcript
- TagSelector component works both as modal content AND inline sidebar content
- Second AI call: generate pearls scoped to selected tags
- Store selected tags per meeting (needed for cumulative tag system)
- `/api/tags` endpoint for tag extraction
- `/api/pearls/generate` endpoint for focused pearl generation

## Data Model
- Tags stored per meeting (both AI-generated and user-selected) in `selected_tags TEXT[]` column
- Support AI-generated and custom user tags

title: Inline title editing from summary view
description:
## User Story
As a user, I want to quickly edit the meeting title directly from the summary view so I can give meetings meaningful names.

## User Quote
> "Something I would like to have is immediately I can edit the title. It would be nice to have, like, a little button to edit so I can title it on my own."

## Requirements
- **Click-to-edit**: Clicking the title text enters edit mode
- **Edit icon**: Small pencil/edit icon also visible next to title as affordance
- Either interaction enters the same inline edit mode
- Save on blur or Enter, cancel on Escape
- Works for both logged-in users (persists to Supabase) and guests (persists to localStorage)

title: Visually distinguish pearls section from summary
description:
## User Story
As a user, I want the pearls section to be visually distinct from the summary so I can quickly differentiate between content types.

## User Quote
> "I was looking at the pearls, and I was like, oh, that's kind of cool, but it blends together with the summary, because it's all white. So I was imagining maybe the like panel for pearls is like slightly different shade."

## Requirements
- Full panel restyle for the pearls sidebar
- Different background shade/color from the summary
- Each pearl gets its own card treatment (border/shadow)
- **Independent scroll** within the pearls sidebar panel (layout is side-by-side with summary)
- Accent color or typography distinction to reinforce the visual separation
- Maintain readability — distinct but not jarring

## Layout
Pearls are displayed as a sidebar next to the summary (side-by-side). The sidebar should scroll independently of the summary content.

title: Context-aware pearl generation (private vs shared)
description:
## User Story
As a user, I want pearls to be generated differently based on whether they're private or shared, so the content matches my intended use case.

## User Quote
> "What I want to see in pearls would also change based on whether this is just going to my dashboard or if it's going to a dashboard that you all can see."

## Requirements
- User indicates whether pearls are for personal or shared consumption
- Private pearls: more personal, introspective, "what did I learn"
- Shared pearls: more collaborative, team-relevant, actionable
- Generation prompt adapts based on intended audience

title: Cumulative tag system across meetings
description:
## User Story
As a user, I want my selected tags to accumulate across meetings so I can build a personal knowledge system of concepts that matter to me.

## User Quote
> "And then they can, like, accumulate with every transcript that I make."

## Requirements
- Tags persist across meetings in the user's profile
- **Dashboard sidebar** displays accumulated tags
- Tags grow over time as more meetings are processed
- User can see which tags recur across meetings and which are new
- Clicking a tag could filter/show related pearls across meetings

## Data Model
- `user_tags` table: tag text, user_id, frequency/count, first_seen, last_seen
- Junction table linking tags to meetings/pearls
- Support both AI-generated and user-created tags

## Dependencies
Blocked by tag-first pearl selection (context-keeper-ggz) — tags must exist per-meeting before they can accumulate.

## Scope
MVP is: persist selected tags, show them in a dashboard sidebar with counts. Advanced features (tag relationships, concept graphs) are future work.

title: Surface personal quotes and team quotes in pearls
description:
## User Story
As a user, I want to see both my own significant quotes and notable team quotes in pearls, so I can capture both personal insights and collaborative moments.

## User Quote
> "I think I would expect to see here, like my quotes, like my significant quotes that I could save... I'm interested in the cool things. I said. Two, I'm interested in cool things. We said."

## Requirements
- Pearls surface the user's own notable quotes ("my insights")
- Pearls also surface significant quotes from other participants ("our insights")
- Clear attribution — who said what
- Visual distinction between personal and team quotes

## Speaker Identification
- **Otter imports**: Auto-match Otter account owner's name to the logged-in user
- **Pasted transcripts**: Try to match logged-in user's display name against speaker labels in the transcript; if no match, fall back to asking the user which speaker they are
- Needs speaker labels to be present in transcript (degrade gracefully if absent)

## Data Model
- Pearl needs a `speaker` field and a `is_user` boolean (or equivalent)
- User identity mapping: Otter owner name → user, or transcript speaker name → user
